findings.evidence: Preface (PDF p.22): "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A" — but the same page also says "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe" and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)"; Ch. 4 Table 4-2 note (PDF p.75): "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios)"; Ch. 1 (PDF p.27): "all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10"; Ch. 3 (PDF p.76): "model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10".
findings.issue: Three mutually inconsistent reference forms are used for one class of target — Appendix A's own section numbers: "§ 9A" (number-then-letter, which the Preface defines as the scheme), "A.3 / A.6 / A.7 / A.10" (letter-then-number) and a bare "§10". Under the convention the Preface states, "§10" and "A.10" do not resolve to a "9A"-style label, and a reader cannot tell whether they name the same section. The same prefix is also used for figure numbers ("Fig A.2") and section numbers ("§A.7"), which compounds the ambiguity. This is a cross-reference defect that will not resolve for a reader navigating Appendix A.
findings.fix_instruction: Choose one appendix-section label scheme (e.g. "§ A.10", "§ A.7") and normalise every occurrence to it — including the Preface's definition of "§ 9A" and the bare "§10" in Ch. 1 — or, if "9A" is a genuinely distinct subsection label, print the full scheme (section number + subsection letter) once in the Preface and map the A.N references onto it.
